params.body:
## Why

The donations page and the newsletter list both opened with one shared token in the address. That token sits in browser history, is the same for everybody, and cannot be taken from one person without changing it for all. The two pages knew each other through a single link, and each carried its own copy of the styles, which had started to differ. The mails the site sends about the newsletter looked like nothing else Afrodidact sends.

## What changes

### Logging in
- `/admin`: type your address, get a mail with a link. The link works once, for 20 minutes, and starts a session of 30 days on that device.
- Opening the link shows a button; only the button logs in. A mail program or scanner that follows links cannot use the link up.
- The form answers the same whether an address has access or not.
- `/admin/access`: who may log in, with access per section (Donations, Newsletter, People with access). New people get all three by default. Removing a person ends their sessions at once.
- One check, `authorize()` in `src/lib/adminAuth.ts`, guards every back-office page and endpoint: `/finance`, `/campaign/<slug>/manage`, `/newsletter-admin`, `/admin/access` and the six endpoints behind them.

### The shared link stays, until switched off
- `?token=<FINANCE_TOKEN>` keeps working for every section. That is how the first person gets in to give themselves access.
- It can be switched off on `/admin/access`, only by someone logged in with their own address, which proves the login by mail works. While it is off, at least one person has to keep "People with access".
- Campaign manager links are not touched.

### What is stored
People, sessions, login links and the one setting live in Sanity under ids with a dot (`adminUser.…`, `adminSession.…`, `adminLogin.…`, `adminSettings.main`), readable only with the token. Sessions and links are stored under the hash of their secret. The cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax and Secure; a request that changes something on the strength of the cookie also has to come from the site's own pages.

No new environment variables.

### One look
- `src/styles/admin.css` and `src/layouts/AdminLayout.astro` serve every back-office page. The look is taken from afrodidact.org: the white bar with the logo, its near-black and greys, its pill buttons and typefaces, and the logo's colours.
- One menu on every page, with only the sections that person may open.
- One way to show a state, one date format (20 Nov 2026), and the logo's colours in the charts.
- The login page shows one of six photos the public site already uses, another on each visit.
- The donations and campaign pages keep their charts, tabs and tables; they lose their copies of the shared styles.

### Mails
`mailLayout()` in `src/lib/email.ts`, modelled on the newsletter: logo, large dark title, red button, grey foot. Used by the newsletter confirmation (NL, FR, EN) and the login mail. `public/images/logo-mail.png` is the logo as a PNG, because many mail programs do not show an SVG. The donation mails keep their own layout.

## Checked

- `npm test`: 95 pass, 15 of them new (ids, sections, where to go after login, comparing secrets, same-site check, the date format).
- `npm run build` passes.
- The whole flow was walked through in a browser, 44 checks: giving access, logging in, a used link being dead, a newsletter-only person refused on donations and its exports, the session refused from another site, switching the shared link off, the last person with access not removable, removing a person ending their session, logging out, an old cookie being worthless, no secret stored as is.
- Every page was looked at on desktop and phone width with made-up donors and subscribers, and both mails in a browser.

## Not checked

- **The real dataset.** The walk-through ran against an in-memory stand-in for Sanity that evaluates the same GROQ. The queries have not run against Sanity itself.
- **A real mail** arriving, and how the new layout looks in Gmail and Outlook.
- The donations page with live Mollie data.

If something is off after deploy, the shared link still works, since it stays on until someone switches it off.

## After merging

1. Open `/admin/access?token=<the finance token>` and give yourself access.
2. Go to `/admin`, ask for a link, log in.
3. Give the others access.
4. When everyone has logged in once, switch the shared link off on that page.

The smoke test now also checks that nothing of the back office or the newsletter list is readable without a login.
params.title: The back office gets a login by mail, one menu and one look
